answer: An agent market requires every trading identity to lock a bond for 30 days, with its credit limit capped at that bond. A public ledger acts as a lantern, exposing how much collateral backs each account. An attacker can grow a vine of fake agents, but each new account needs fresh locked capital; splitting one bond adds no total credit. Even at the nadir of interest rates, the attacker must fund the full collateral and forgo its use elsewhere.
